event_name: Mora royal commission executes twenty-three witches
significance: A royal commission convened at Mora, Sweden, in 1669 accepted the testimony of approximately three hundred children reporting mass abductions to the Blåkulla sabbath and resulted in twenty-three executions, triggering the broader Swedish witch panic of 1668-1676 and representing the most intense use of child testimony as the primary prosecutorial mechanism in European witch-hunting.
source_method: Royal commission records; analyzed in Ankarloo and Henningsen, Early Modern European Witchcraft (1990) and Behringer, Witches and Witch-Hunts (2004)
